device.name: Xiaomi Mijia LYWSD03MMC Thermometer/Hygrometer
device.notes:
Compact BLE thermometer and hygrometer with E-ink display. Telink TLSR8251 SoC, CR2032 battery, 6-12 month battery life. $4-6. 6 hardware versions: B1.4, B1.5, B1.6, B1.7, B1.9, B2.0.
STOCK FIRMWARE: broadcasts Xiaomi MiBeacon format (service UUID 0xFE95) with encrypted payload, decryptable only with the unit's bindkey. Two routes to that key: extract the one Mi Home's cloud issued, or set a NEW one with the pvvx Telink Flasher's activation, keeping the stock firmware. Home Assistant's Xiaomi BLE documentation names exactly five models for the pvvx route (LYWSD03MMC, MJWSD05MMC, MHO-C401, CGG1, CGDK2) and the atc1441 flasher as an alternative for an unstated wider set. After a flasher activation Mi Home no longer recognises the sensor; to use Mi Home again, remove and re-add it there. Key length follows the MiBeacon version: v2/v3 take a 12-byte key (24 hex characters), v4/v5 a 16-byte key (32 hex characters) with authenticated encryption — a key of the wrong length for the beacon version is the usual import mistake. REPORTED from that documentation; no activation or key write was performed by this project.
CUSTOM FIRMWARE (recommended for local control): the pvvx/ATC_MiThermometer project provides OTA-flashable firmware (via web browser at https://pvvx.github.io/ATC_MiThermometer/TelinkMiFlasher.html) that:
  - Broadcasts unencrypted temperature/humidity/battery
  - Supports 4 advertisement formats: ATC, Xiaomi, Custom, BTHome v2
  - Has configurable advertising interval and TX power
  - Provides GATT connection mode for configuration
  - Supports encrypted beacons with PIN-code or bindkey
  - Exposes standard Device Information (0x180A) and Battery (0x180F) services
  - Supports BLE 5.0+ LE Long Range (Coded PHY S=8)

UNENCRYPTED ATC (atc1441) ADVERTISEMENT FORMAT — Service Data UUID 0x181A:
  bytes 0-5: MAC (big-endian)
  bytes 6-7: temperature int16 BE, ×0.1 °C
  byte 8: humidity %
  byte 9: battery %
  bytes 10-11: battery mV (uint16 BE)
  byte 12: advertisement counter

UNENCRYPTED PVVX CUSTOM ADVERTISEMENT FORMAT — same 0x181A UUID, 14-15 B (14 without trigger/status flags, 15 with them):
  bytes 0-5: MAC
  bytes 6-7: temperature int16 LE, ×0.01 °C
  bytes 8-9: humidity uint16 LE, ×0.01 %
  bytes 10-11: battery mV (uint16)
  byte 12: battery %
  byte 13: advertisement counter
  byte 14: trigger/status flags
(custom_beacon.h adv_atc1441_t / adv_custom_t)
ENCRYPTED ATC/Custom BEACONS: AES-CCM with bindkey (16 bytes), nonce = MAC (6 bytes) + header (5 bytes), auth data = 0x11, MAC len = 4. The 5-byte header is the advertisement's own AD-structure head: length, AD type 0x16 (Service Data), UUID16 0x181A as its little-endian bytes 1a 18, then the frame counter (pvvx/ATC_MiThermometer; reported). The decrypted plaintexts are the compact 3-byte (temp=(v/2)-40 °C, hum=v/2 %, battery bits 6-0 + trigger bit 7) and 6-byte (temp int16 LE 0.01 °C, humi uint16 LE 0.01 %, battery %, flags) layouts in payload_formats below — those two layouts do NOT appear on the air unencrypted.
GATT CONNECTION (custom firmware): device advertises as "ATC_XXXXXX" (where XXXXXX are last 3 bytes of MAC). Standard services:
  0x180A — Device Information (manufacturer, model, firmware version)
  0x180F — Battery Service (battery level)
Configuration is done via proprietary characteristics on the ATC service. Set defaults command: write 0x56, disable Long Range: write 0xDD.
ALSO SUPPORTS: MHO-C401/C401N, MJWSD05MMC, Qingping CGG1-M/CGDK2, Tuya TH03/ZTH01/02/05 — all with same custom firmware and Telink SoC.
CURRENT STATUS (verified 2026-07-31): custom firmware v5.8 defaults to the BTHome v2 advertisement format. The same hardware converts to Zigbee via pvvx/ZigbeeTLc (Z03MMC). Units sold since 2025-03 with PCB marks B1.5*/B1.6* use SPI LCD controllers and cheaper clone sensors, drawing more current with a low-contrast display — pvvx currently advises against buying LYWSD03MMC (ATC_MiThermometer issue #664). Those boards are still supported by the custom firmware (under the internal number B1.1, to tell them from the older B1.6), but new B1.6 units ship an original firmware (2.1.1_0159) that is incompatible with every older hardware version, and their first OTA needs Mi Home registration (issue #602). Upstream counts only B1.4, B1.7, B1.9 and B2.0 as normal hardware.
LATEST RELEASE (checked 2026-11-11): pvvx release 5.9 (firmware.json at commit b02b5137, 2026-11-02), which fixes an error in the initial OTA download at address 0x40000. The hardware-tested unit ran 5.8; whether 5.9 changes any default was not checked.
STOCK FIRMWARE DISCOVERY: name "LYWSD03MMC", service UUID 0xFE95 (MiBeacon), random address (custom firmware uses the public address; pvvx, reported). Data is encrypted; decryption requires the bindkey — the Mi Home-issued one, or one set by Telink Flasher activation.
MI HOME APP EVIDENCE (static-analysis audit, 2026-08): the app contains NO device-specific code for this model — Mi Home device plugins are downloaded from Xiaomi's cloud at pairing time, and "LYWSD03MMC" is entirely absent from the app (code and bundled assets alike), so the app can only corroborate generic Xiaomi mechanisms, nothing model-specific. What it does confirm:
  - MiBeacon service UUID 0xFE95 and the frame-control layout: bytes
    0-1 are a little-endian frame-control field (bit 3 = payload
    encrypted, plus capability/MAC/event/binding flag bits) and the
    version sits in the high nibble of byte 1
    (from its MiBeacon service-data parser).
  - During provisioning the app pushes the cloud-issued bindkey to
    the device via a miio RPC with method "set_bind_key" (params
    carry bind_key plus Wi-Fi credentials)
    (from its provisioning bind-key step).
  - The bundled device catalog (assets/device_config/plugin_config_us-en)
    lists MiOT model "miaomiaoce.sensor_ht.t2" (pd_id 1371, "Mi
    Temperature and Humidity Monitor 2" — this device's retail name),
    its Mi Home/MiOT identity; no plugin or logic for it ships in the
    app itself.
CONFIDENCE for the app-evidence block: MEDIUM — app-derived, not verified on hardware.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH for custom firmware advertisement formats, service UUIDs, and GATT services — sourced from github.com/pvvx/ATC_MiThermometer and confirmed by Home Assistant Passive BLE Monitor, BTHome, and other integrations. Stock firmware MiBeacon format documented by Xiaomi but encrypted payload requires a bindkey (cloud-issued, or set by the Telink Flasher). Firmware is OTA-flashable and reversible, provided the original image matches the hardware generation (see features.firmware_update).

pairing.notes: Nothing bonds on either firmware — this is a broadcast sensor, and no client ever pairs with it at the link layer. What the stock firmware requires is a key, not a pairing: its MiBeacon payload is encrypted, and the bindkey comes from the Mi Home account the thermometer is registered to, or from a Telink Flasher activation that sets a new one. The recommended path here is the pvvx/ATC custom firmware, which broadcasts unencrypted and has no account, no key and no pairing of any kind; the flash is reversible.

pin.notes: Stock firmware only, and not a PIN: the MiBeacon bindkey that decrypts the broadcast payload, extracted once from the Mi Home app — or, instead, a new one written by the pvvx Telink Flasher's activation (setup.methods). Per-unit, so no value appears here. Custom firmware removes the need for it entirely.

unpair.clears: The Xiaomi account binding, and with it the validity of the extracted bindkey.
unpair.notes: Removing the thermometer from Mi Home invalidates the bindkey, so a local integration that was decoding broadcasts stops decoding them with no change on its own side. Re-pairing issues a new one. Flashing the custom firmware makes the whole question moot.

issued_to_client: Bindkey (stock firmware, obtained from Xiaomi cloud via Mi Home, or set by Telink Flasher activation)
credentials.notes: Custom firmware stores no cloud credentials. Optional PIN for GATT access control. A bindkey set by the Telink Flasher replaces the Mi Home one, and re-adding the sensor to Mi Home afterwards may replace it again (reported, not tested here).
stored_on_device: Bindkey (stock firmware, for MiBeacon encryption; 12 bytes for MiBeacon v2/v3, 16 bytes for v4/v5)

factory_reset.effect: Clears bindkey, PIN, comfort settings, and measurement history. Returns to custom firmware defaults.

steps.action: Connect to ATC_XXXXXX device via GATT.
Remove CR2032 battery for 10+ seconds, then reinsert.

methods.description: Flash custom firmware via web browser OTA to enable direct unencrypted BLE advertisement of temperature, humidity, and battery without Xiaomi cloud dependency.
methods.name: Flash custom firmware over Web Bluetooth

steps.action: Click 'Connect' and select LYWSD03MMC from the browser BLE chooser.
Click 'Do Activation' to run the activation and decryption-key step; the first flash from stock firmware cannot skip it.

steps.expect: Device reboots and advertises as ATC_XXXXXX. A transfer takes about four minutes; if it is interrupted the device keeps its old firmware (upstream README).

methods.description: Keep the stock MiBeacon firmware but replace its bindkey with a new one from the pvvx Telink Flasher's activation, instead of extracting the Mi Home-issued key. Home Assistant's Xiaomi BLE documentation names this route for LYWSD03MMC, MJWSD05MMC, MHO-C401, CGG1 and CGDK2, and the atc1441 flasher as an alternative for an unstated wider set (which does not extend the explicit five-model list). Reported from that documentation; not exercised by this project, and the 2.1.1_0159 / new-B1.6 case is unconfirmed (remaining_unknowns).
methods.name: Keep stock firmware, set your own bindkey with the Telink Flasher

steps.action: Open TelinkMiFlasher.html in Chrome/Edge/Opera, click 'Connect' and choose the LYWSD03MMC.
Click 'Do Activation'; record the bindkey the flasher reports, and do not flash any firmware.
steps.expect: The sensor keeps broadcasting encrypted MiBeacon frames, now under the new key.

steps.action: Enter the key into the decoding client, matching its length to the MiBeacon version (12 bytes for v2/v3, 16 bytes for v4/v5).
If Mi Home will be used again, remove the sensor from Mi Home and add it back; the decoding client's key may then need updating.
steps.expect: Mi Home recognises the sensor again only after it is re-added.

cloud.local_alternative: Flash custom firmware for fully local control.

methods.description: Alternative: pair with Xiaomi Mi Home app to obtain bindkey, then use stock firmware with encrypted MiBeacon decryption.
methods.name: Keep stock firmware, take the bindkey from Mi Home

setup.notes:
STOCK FIRMWARE needs a bindkey: either the one Mi Home's cloud issues at pairing (extracted afterwards), or a new one set by the pvvx Telink Flasher's activation, which Home Assistant documents as an alternative to cloud extraction. It leaves Mi Home unable to recognise the sensor until it is removed and re-added there, and it is not evidence that every hardware revision is account-free: the 2.1.1_0159 units need Mi Home registration before their first OTA (below). CUSTOM FIRMWARE eliminates the key entirely — flash via web browser OTA from https://pvvx.github.io/ATC_MiThermometer/TelinkMiFlasher.html (Chrome/Edge/Opera with Experimental Web Platform features enabled). Firmware change is reversible (original firmware images available), but only with the original image for the unit's hardware generation: 1.0.0_0130 covers the older B1.4-B2.0 boards, and new B1.6 units use the 2.1.1_0159 line, which is incompatible with older hardware. Let the flasher's hardware detection choose, not a filename. The first flash from stock firmware always goes through TelinkMiFlasher's activation; later updates of a unit already on custom firmware can use any Telink OTA client. After flashing, device advertises as "ATC_XXXXXX" with unencrypted data.
Battery must be >40% for reliable OTA flashing on LYWSD03MMC.
LOCKDOWN CAVEAT: devices shipping stock firmware 2.1.1_0159 require Mi Home registration plus an extracted Mi token/bindkey (e.g. via Xiaomi-cloud-tokens-extractor) before the TelinkMiFlasher OTA works — the unauthenticated stock OTA was closed by Xiaomi, so the cloud-free flashing path no longer holds for recent stock (ATC_MiThermometer issue #602).

rejoin.notes: Custom firmware: scan for ATC_XXXXXX. Stock: requires Mi Home re-pairing.

testing.notes: One unit running the pvvx ATC custom firmware v5.8 was scanned and connected on 2026-08-22 (Linux/BlueZ, bleak). What was exercised: the BTHome v2 advertisement under service data 0xFCD2 (decoded battery 92 %, 23.81 degrees C, 59.93 % RH) and the connected GATT table (Device Information reporting manufacturer miaomiaoce.com, model LYWSD03MMC, firmware github.com/pvvx; environmental service 0x181A with 2a1f/2a6e/2a6f, whose reads matched the advertised values). That is the whole of it — the payload_formats for stock firmware, the atc1441 and pvvx-custom advertisement layouts, the comfort/ config writes and the history buffer were NOT exercised, and the other firmware variants in device.variants were not on hand.

variants.notes: Custom firmware. 6 hardware versions. Name format: ATC_XXXXXX — in BTHome format (v5.8 default) the name may arrive only in the scan response, so name-less advertisements are normal; match 0xFCD2 there.
Stock firmware with encrypted MiBeacon. Service UUID 0xFE95.
Custom firmware advertises as MHO_XXXXXX (ble_set_name in ble.c).
Custom firmware advertises as MHO_XXXXXX, same prefix as MHO-C401.
Custom firmware advertises as BTH_XXXXXX; English-hardware units use BTE_.

evidence.documentation_review: 2026-11-11: the Home Assistant Xiaomi BLE encryption documentation, the pvvx/ATC_MiThermometer README and firmware.json at commit b02b5137 and issue #602 were read for the bindkey-provisioning route, the key-length rule, the hardware-generation warnings and the 5.9 release. Four public BLE images were downloaded and hashed; none was flashed, and no activation, bindkey write or Mi Home login was performed. Everything taken from these sources is reported, not confirmed. The earlier hardware session (2026-08-22, pvvx 5.8) is described under device.testing.

enter.notes: The Telink stack default: the running firmware receives the image and reboots into it at the end (firmware-update.md). The flasher runs 'Do Activation' before flashing on stock firmware.

image.notes:
pvvx custom firmware and the original stock images are both available through https://pvvx.github.io/ATC_MiThermometer/TelinkMiFlasher.html (source at github.com/pvvx/ATC_MiThermometer), which is what makes the change reversible. Unsigned in the sense that matters: the custom build installs, so nothing verifies a vendor signature. Stock firmware 2.1.1_0159 gates the OTA session instead — Mi Home registration and an extracted Mi token/bindkey first (ATC_MiThermometer issue #602).
The original image must match the hardware generation: upstream ships 1.0.0_0130 for the older B1.4-B2.0 boards and a separate 2.1.1_0159 line for new B1.6 units, incompatible with older hardware. The flasher's manifest (firmware.json, release 5.9) also carries a "signed" list naming a 2.1.1_0159c original image; what that signature is and whether new-B1.6 stock firmware checks it before accepting an image is not established (remaining_unknowns), so `signing: unsigned` is asserted for the custom-firmware path, not for every stock bootloader. Images larger than 128 KB (Ext.OTA) are not supported. Pinned digests of the four public images are in evidence.artifacts.

dfu.notes: From the pvvx/ATC_MiThermometer project and its TelinkMiFlasher page; the flash itself was not exercised by this project (the tested unit already ran v5.8). The Telink OTA service UUID the flasher uses is in registries/dfu-signatures.tsv; it is not recorded in this spec's GATT table, so it is not listed under `services`. After flashing the device advertises as "ATC_XXXXXX". A unit already running the custom firmware can also be updated without a browser by the project's utils/ble_ota.py (Python, bleak), which reads the hardware and firmware version and flashes the firmware.json release image for that hardware only when the unit is older; the first flash from stock firmware still needs TelinkMiFlasher's activation (upstream README at commit b02b5137).

recovery.notes: The Telink stack default (the new image goes to the other flash bank and the boot flag switches only on success), and now also stated by the upstream README for this firmware: an interrupted transfer (about four minutes) leaves the old firmware running. Not checked on a unit here. Keep the battery above 40 % for a reliable flash.

ATC_3byte.description: 3-byte ATC layout. NOTE: this compact layout exists only as the AES-CCM PLAINTEXT of the ENCRYPTED ATC beacon (adv_atc_data_t in custom_beacon.h) — it never appears on the air unencrypted. The unencrypted on-air ATC format is ATC_atc1441 below.

ATC_atc1441.description: Unencrypted on-air ATC advertisement (adv_atc1441_t in custom_beacon.h), Service Data 0x181A.

BTHome_v2.description: BTHome v2 advertisement, the pvvx firmware default since v5.8 and so the layout most units are actually broadcasting. Carried as Service Data under 0xFCD2, NOT 0x181A — 0x181A appears only in the connected GATT table on a BTHome-configured unit. Unlike the four layouts above this one is TLV, not fixed: byte 0 is the BTHome device-info byte (0x40 = v2, unencrypted) and the rest is a run of [object id][value] pairs in ascending id order. The indices below are the run this firmware emits; a general decoder should walk the ids rather than trust the offsets, because a field the device has nothing to report is simply absent. Hardware-verified 2026-08-22 on pvvx v5.8 (decoded 92 %, 23.81 °C, 59.93 % RH, matching the values read back over GATT in the same session).

fields.description: BTHome device-info byte. 0x40 = BTHome v2, unencrypted, no trigger.
fields.name: device_info

parse_rules: Reject the frame unless byte[0] == 0x40; any other value means a BTHome variant this table does not describe (encrypted, or a different version).
Walk from byte 1: read an object id, then its value, whose width the id fixes (0x00 packet id = 1 byte, 0x01 battery = 1 byte, 0x02 temperature = 2 bytes, 0x03 humidity = 2 bytes).
The example is the verified reading (battery 0x5c = 92 %, temp 0x094d = 23.81 C, humidity 0x1769 = 59.93 %) with the packet counter written ?? because it changes every advertisement.

Custom_unencrypted.description: Unencrypted on-air Custom (pvvx) advertisement (adv_custom_t in custom_beacon.h), Service Data 0x181A: 14 bytes without trigger/status flags, 15 bytes when the optional flags byte is present.

fields.description: Advertisement counter; a flags byte follows on 15-byte frames.
fields.name: counter

PVVX_6byte.description: 6-byte Custom layout. NOTE: as with ATC_3byte, this is the AES-CCM PLAINTEXT of the ENCRYPTED Custom beacon (adv_cust_data_t in custom_beacon.h) — the unencrypted on-air Custom format is Custom_unencrypted below.

remaining_unknowns: Whether the pvvx Telink Flasher can set a new bindkey on a stock 2.1.1_0159 / new-B1.6 unit without Mi Home registration first; issue #602 says that firmware's first OTA needs Mi Home registration and IDs, and the bindkey-only route was not tested.

Whether a decoding client's bindkey has to be re-entered after the sensor is removed from and re-added to Mi Home following a flasher activation (Home Assistant's documentation implies the Mi Home re-add; the key consequence was not tested).
Which models the atc1441 alternative flasher can re-key; the Home Assistant documentation calls the set broader than the pvvx five but does not list it.
What the 'signed' list in the flasher's firmware.json (the 2.1.1_0159c original image) means — whose signature, and whether new-B1.6 stock firmware refuses an image without it.
Whether release 5.9 changes any default (advertising format, interval) relative to the hardware-tested 5.8.

characteristics.name: Temperature
characteristics.notes: SIG Temperature characteristic as the pvvx custom firmware exposes it: int16 little-endian in 0.01 degrees C. HARDWARE: a read of this characteristic on a v5.8 unit matched the value the same unit was advertising (see device.testing), so the layout is confirmed.

characteristics.name: Humidity
characteristics.notes: SIG Humidity characteristic: uint16 little-endian in 0.01 percent relative humidity. Confirmed the same way as 2a6e — the GATT read agreed with the advertised humidity on the tested unit.

services.name: Environmental Sensing Service
services.notes: Used in advertisement Service Data for ATC custom firmware beacon broadcasts, AND exposed as a real GATT service by the custom firmware (app_att.c): Temperature 0x2A6E and Humidity 0x2A6F, both read + notify. Data is therefore available either from passive BLE scanning of the advertisement payload or over a GATT connection.

services.name: Device Information Service
services.notes: Standard BLE Device Information. Exposed by custom firmware v1.5+ when connected via GATT. Provides manufacturer name, model number, serial number, firmware revision, hardware revision, and software revision.

characteristics.name: Battery Level
characteristics.notes: SIG Battery Level: one unsigned byte, 0-100 percent. The custom firmware also enables notify on it (pvvx/ATC_MiThermometer, app_att.c) even though only read was exercised here.

services.name: Battery Service
services.notes: Standard BLE Battery Service. Exposed by custom firmware.
